question: Average function is listed in the drop-down menu of which of the following tools?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Auto Sum function.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel, the AutoSum button (Σ) on the Home/Formulas tab has a drop-down arrow that reveals several common functions besides SUM: Average, Count Numbers, Max, and Min. (औसत फलन — ऑटो सम फलन)

 

• Clicking the small arrow next to the AutoSum button opens this list, letting a user quickly insert AVERAGE(), COUNT(), MAX() or MIN() without typing the formula manually.

 

• The AVERAGE function itself calculates the arithmetic mean of a selected range of numeric cells.

 

• This drop-down menu is a shortcut feature meant to speed up common calculations for spreadsheet users.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Financial functions, Move, and Insert are located elsewhere in Excel's ribbon/menus and are unrelated to the AutoSum drop-down.

 

NOTE

 

• Financial function (Option 1): A separate category under the Formulas tab for functions like PMT, FV, NPV, etc., not part of the AutoSum menu.

 

• Move function (Option 3): Not a standard Excel function/category name.

 

• Insert function (Option 4): Refers to the "Insert Function" dialog (fx button) used to search all Excel functions, not specifically the AutoSum drop-down.

question: Where can you find the emoticons in an instant messaging conversation window?
option_1: At the middle of the chat window
option_2: Any where in the chat window
option_3: At the bottom of the chat window
option_4: At the top of the chat window
solution_text:
The correct answer is At the bottom of the chat window.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In most instant messaging (IM) applications, emoticon/emoji icons are placed at the bottom of the chat window, next to the message-typing/input box. (इमोटिकॉन आइकन — चैट विंडो के नीचे)

 

• This placement lets users quickly insert emojis right before sending a message, keeping the conversation flow smooth.

 

• The chat display area (message history) occupies the upper/middle portion, while the toolbar (attachments, emoji, send button) sits along the bottom edge.

 

• This convention is followed across common IM/chat apps and browser-based chat interfaces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar bottom-bar placement is used for attachment and send icons in most messaging UIs.

 

NOTE

 

• At the middle (Option 1): The message history occupies the middle, not the toolbar.

 

• Anywhere (Option 2): Emoticon placement is fixed near the input box, not random.

 

• At the top (Option 4): The top typically shows the contact name/status, not emoticons.

question: Who has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parliament.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 11 of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law, notwithstanding anything in the preceding provisions of Part II (Articles 5-10). (नागरिकता अधिकार का विनियमन — संसद)

 

• Under this power, Parliament enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955, which lays down provisions for the acquisition and termination of citizenship.

 

• Parliament has since amended this Act multiple times, e.g. the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019.

 

• Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5-11) deals with citizenship as it stood at the commencement of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Citizenship Act 1955 recognises acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.

 

NOTE

 

• Supreme Court (Option 1): Interprets citizenship law in disputes but does not have the power to make/regulate it.

 

• President (Option 2): Assents to laws passed by Parliament; does not independently regulate citizenship.

 

• Governor (Option 3): A state-level constitutional head with no role in citizenship, which is a Union subject.

question: In which year has India hosted the Asian Games for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 in New Delhi. (एशियाई खेल — 1951, नई दिल्ली)

 

• These were the inaugural edition of the Asian Games, held at the National Stadium, New Delhi, from 4 to 11 March 1951.

 

• 489 athletes from 11 countries participated across 6 sports.

 

• India has since hosted the Asian Games a second time, in 1982 (also in New Delhi).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Asian Games are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA), every four years.

 

• The 2023 Asian Games (19th edition) were held in Hangzhou, China.

 

NOTE

 

• 1948 (Option 1): Year of the London Olympics, not the Asian Games.

 

• 1950 (Option 3) / 1949 (Option 4): No Asian Games edition was held in these years; the first edition took place in 1951.

question: Who among the following was the author of ‘Brihat Katha Kosh’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harisena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Brihatkathakosha' (Brihat Katha Kosh) is a 10th-century Jain text written in Sanskrit by Harisena in 931 CE. (बृहत्कथा कोश — हरिषेण)

 

• It is a collection of stories illustrating Jain religious and moral principles, composed while Harisena was residing in the Vardhamana Prasada mandapa at Wardha (Maharashtra).

 

• The text provides valuable insights into the contemporary society, religion and geography of that era.

 

• It is written in Sanskrit prose interspersed with verse.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original 'Brihatkatha' (a lost Paishachi Prakrit epic) is attributed to Gunadhya; later Sanskrit adaptations include Kshemendra's 'Brihatkathamanjari' and Somadeva's 'Kathasaritsagara'.

 

NOTE

 

• Dandin (Option 1): Author of 'Dashakumaracharita' and 'Kavyadarsha', a Sanskrit prose writer, unrelated to Brihat Katha Kosh.

 

• Kshemendra (Option 3): Wrote 'Brihatkathamanjari', a different adaptation of Brihatkatha, not Brihat Katha Kosh.

 

• Bhavabhuti (Option 4): A renowned Sanskrit dramatist (Uttararamacharita, Malatimadhava), unrelated to this text.

question: Langvir Nritya is a folk dance from the state of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Langvir Nritya is an acrobatic folk dance of the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, traditionally performed only by men. (लंगवीर नृत्य — उत्तराखंड)

 

• Dancers climb a long wooden pole and perform daring acrobatic feats/postures at the top and while descending, showcasing balance and physical skill.

 

• It is usually performed during festivals and fairs, especially in Tehri Garhwal district, to celebrate the harvest season.

 

• The dance symbolises valour, agility and community celebration among Garhwali men.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Uttarakhand include Chholiya and Jhumailo.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Known for dances like Dhamal and Phag, not Langvir Nritya.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Known for Raslila and Kajri, not Langvir Nritya.

question: Geoid is the ________ of earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is shape.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Geoid is defined as the true physical shape of the Earth — an equipotential surface that coincides with mean sea level extended hypothetically under the continents. (जिओइड — पृथ्वी का आकार)

 

• It is irregular (not a perfect sphere or ellipsoid) because Earth's mass distribution is uneven, causing local gravitational variation.

 

• The geoid is used as the reference surface for measuring precise elevations/heights in geodesy.

 

• It differs from the reference ellipsoid used for GPS calculations, which is a simplified mathematical model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Earth's actual shape is often described as an "oblate spheroid" — flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator — while the geoid captures the exact undulating shape defined by gravity.

 

NOTE

 

• Axis (Option 2): Refers to Earth's imaginary line of rotation, not its shape.

 

• Colour (Option 3): The geoid is a geometric/gravitational concept, unrelated to colour.

 

• Orbit (Option 4): Refers to Earth's path around the Sun, a separate concept from its shape.

question: In the context of DNA, which of the following principles governs the process of transcription?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The principle of complementarity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Transcription is the process by which a single strand of mRNA is synthesised from a DNA template strand, guided by the principle of base-pair complementarity (A pairs with U, T pairs with A, G pairs with C). (पूरकता का सिद्धांत — प्रतिलेखन)

 

• RNA polymerase reads the DNA template strand 3'→5' and synthesises the complementary RNA strand 5'→3', ensuring the mRNA sequence matches the coding (sense) strand except T is replaced by U.

 

• This complementary base pairing ensures accurate transfer of genetic information from DNA to RNA.

 

• The enzyme RNA polymerase catalyses this process without needing a primer, unlike DNA replication.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DNA replication (a related but distinct process) also relies on complementary base pairing but follows the semiconservative model discovered by Meselson and Stahl.

 

NOTE

 

• The transforming principle (Option 1): Discovered by Griffith/Avery, refers to genetic transformation via DNA uptake by bacteria, unrelated to transcription mechanics.

 

• Semiconservative nature of DNA (Option 3): Describes how DNA replicates (each new DNA molecule has one old and one new strand), not transcription.

 

• The principle of inheritance (Option 4): Refers to Mendelian laws of heredity, unrelated to molecular transcription.

question: With which of the following states is the Bhatiali folk music, which is mostly sung by the fishermen, associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhatiali is a traditional folk music genre of Bengal, sung mainly by boatmen and fishermen while rowing along rivers. (भाटियाली लोकगीत — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• The word "Bhatiali" derives from "bhata" (ebb tide), reflecting songs sung while boats drift downstream with the tide/current.

 

• It expresses themes of longing and the rhythm of river life, often sung in a long, melancholic, drawn-out melodic style.

 

• Bhatiali songs are prevalent in the riverine regions of West Bengal (and historically Bengal on both sides of the India-Bangladesh border).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk music traditions of West Bengal include Baul (mystic minstrel songs) and Bhawaiya (a related genre associated more with North Bengal/Assam cart-drivers).

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for folk forms like Pala and Daskathia, not Bhatiali.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Known for Burrakatha folk narrative singing.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for Vanchipattu (boat songs) — a different regional boat-song tradition, not Bhatiali.

question: Who was the founder of Arya Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dayanand Saraswati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay (Mumbai) on 7 April 1875. (आर्य समाज — दयानंद सरस्वती)

 

• It was a Hindu reform movement based on the infallibility of the Vedas, promoting monotheism and opposing idol worship, caste discrimination and child marriage.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati authored 'Satyarth Prakash', laying out the core philosophy of Arya Samaj.

 

• The movement later shifted its headquarters to Lahore and played a significant role in India's social reform and nationalist movements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other socio-religious reform movements include Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy) and Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda).

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 1): Nobel laureate poet and founder of Visva-Bharati University, unrelated to Arya Samaj.

 

• Keshub Chandra Sen (Option 3): A leader of Brahmo Samaj, not Arya Samaj.

 

• Swami Vivekananda (Option 4): Founder of the Ramakrishna Mission, a disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, unrelated to Arya Samaj's founding.

question: Daler Mehndi is primarily a famous singer of pop songs in which Indian language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjabi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Daler Mehndi is a renowned Indian singer, best known for popularising Punjabi pop music in India during the 1990s. (दलेर मेहंदी — पंजाबी पॉप)

 

• His album 'Bolo Ta Ra Ra' (1995) and hit song 'Tunak Tunak Tun' brought Punjabi pop to mainstream Indian audiences.

 

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2009 for his contribution to Indian music.

 

• He is also known for singing Bhangra-infused dance numbers that became widely popular across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• His brother, Mika Singh, is also a prominent Punjabi/Bollywood playback singer.

 

NOTE

 

• English (Option 1), Hindi (Option 3), Bengali (Option 4): While Daler Mehndi has occasionally sung in other languages/for Bollywood, he is primarily identified as a Punjabi pop singer.

question:
The five-year plans for India with their duration are given below. Which of the following is correctly matched?

(a) Second five-year plan — 1956-57 to 1960-61

(b) Third five-year plan — 1961-62 to 1965-66

(c) Fourth five-year plan — 1966-67 to 1970-71
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both a and b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The actual duration of India's Five-Year Plans: Second Plan (1956-61), Third Plan (1961-66), and Fourth Plan (1969-74). (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं — a और b सही)

 

• Statement (a) is correct: The Second Five-Year Plan ran from 1956-57 to 1960-61 (i.e., 1956-61), focusing on rapid industrialisation based on the Mahalanobis model.

 

• Statement (b) is correct: The Third Five-Year Plan ran from 1961-62 to 1965-66 (i.e., 1961-66), aiming at self-reliant economic growth but was disrupted by the 1962 and 1965 wars and droughts.

 

• Statement (c) is incorrect: The Fourth Five-Year Plan actually ran from 1969-70 to 1973-74 (1969-74), not 1966-67 to 1970-71. The period 1966-69 was instead a "Plan Holiday" of three Annual Plans due to the aftermath of wars, devaluation of the rupee, and drought.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

 

• Five-Year Plans in India were discontinued after the 12th Plan (2012-17); NITI Aayog now issues strategy documents instead.

 

NOTE

 

• Both a and c (Option 1): Incorrect because statement (c) is wrong — the Fourth Plan's actual period was 1969-74, not 1966-71.

 

• Both b and c (Option 2): Incorrect because it omits correct statement (a) and includes incorrect statement (c).

 

• Only a (Option 3): Incorrect because it omits statement (b), which is also correct.

question: Which of the following states/UTs has the first 100% fully digital literate Panchayat in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pullampara Grama Panchayat in Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, was declared India's first 100% fully digital literate panchayat. (डिजिटल साक्षर पंचायत — केरल)

 

• This was achieved as part of Kerala's broader digital literacy mission, building on the state's earlier distinction of being India's first fully (traditionally) literate state.

 

• The initiative involved training every eligible resident of the panchayat in basic digital skills — using smartphones, internet, digital payments, etc.

 

• Kerala has consistently led national indices in literacy and digital inclusion programmes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala was declared India's first fully literate state in 1991 (Ernakulam district was the first fully literate district in India, 1990).

 

• Kerala has also pursued 'complete digital state' initiatives such as the K-FON project for universal internet access.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1): A Union Territory with municipal governance rather than a panchayat system; not linked with this achievement.

 

• Puducherry (Option 2): Recognised for other literacy/administrative achievements, not this specific panchayat distinction.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Not associated with this particular first.

question: Former minister of the state and former president of BJP alliance partner IPFT _____________ received the Padma Shri award (posthumously) in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Chandra Debbarma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Narendra Chandra Debbarma, a former Tripura state minister and former president of the Indigenous People's Front of Tripura (IPFT) — a BJP alliance partner — was conferred the Padma Shri (posthumously) in 2023 for public affairs. (पद्म श्री 2023 — नरेंद्र चंद्र देबबर्मा)

 

• IPFT is a regional political party representing tribal interests in Tripura and has been an alliance partner of the BJP-led state government.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred for distinguished contribution in various fields.

 

• The 2023 Padma Awards were announced on the eve of Republic Day (25 January 2023).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable 2023 Padma Shri awardees from India's Northeast honoured grassroots public service and community contributions.

 

NOTE

 

• Prabhat Choudhury (Option 1), Rebati Mohan Das (Option 3), Pinaki Das Chowdhury (Option 4): None of these individuals was the IPFT-linked posthumous Padma Shri recipient of 2023 — that distinction belongs specifically to Narendra Chandra Debbarma.

question: Sakewa is a religious festival celebrated by the Kirat Khambu Rai community of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sakewa (also spelled Sakela) is a major religious/agricultural festival of the Kirat Khambu Rai community, prominently celebrated in Sikkim. (साकेवा पर्व — सिक्किम)

 

• It is celebrated twice a year — Ubhauli (during the sowing season, spring) and Udhauli (during the harvest season, autumn) — to worship nature and seek blessings for prosperity.

 

• The festival involves the traditional Sakela dance, performed in a circular formation depicting the movements of nature and wildlife.

 

• The Kirat Rai community, of Tibeto-Burman origin, is one of the prominent indigenous communities of Sikkim and neighbouring Himalayan regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim is also home to other important community festivals such as Losar (Bhutia) and Chasok Tangnam (Limbu).

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 1), Himachal Pradesh (Option 3), Goa (Option 4): These states have their own distinct tribal/local festivals, but Sakewa is specifically associated with the Kirat Khambu Rai community of Sikkim.

question: The growth rate of India’s population has been declining since _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1981.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's decadal population growth rate rose continuously until the 1981 Census, after which it has been declining. (जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर में गिरावट — 1981 से)

 

• As per Census data, the decadal growth rate peaked around 1971-81 (24.66%) and has shown a declining trend in each subsequent decade (1981-91: 23.87%; 1991-2001: 21.54%; 2001-11: 17.7%).

 

• This decline reflects the impact of family planning programmes, rising literacy (especially female literacy), and improving socio-economic development.

 

• Despite the declining growth rate, India's population continues to increase in absolute numbers due to its large population base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India conducted its first Census in 1872 (first synchronous Census in 1881); the Census is conducted every 10 years.

 

• India overtook China to become the world's most populous country in 2023, as per UN estimates.

 

NOTE

 

• 1971 (Option 1): The growth rate was actually still rising up to and including the 1971-81 decade, not declining from 1971.

 

• 1991 (Option 2): The decline had already begun a decade earlier, from 1981.

 

• 1951 (Option 3): The growth rate trend was rising, not declining, through most decades after 1951.

question: As of March 2024, who among the following is the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prakash Shrivastava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Prakash Shrivastava, former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, took charge as the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) in August 2023 and continued to hold the post as of March 2024. (राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण अध्यक्ष — प्रकाश श्रीवास्तव)

 

• The NGT is a specialised judicial body established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection.

 

• He succeeded Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel, who had completed his tenure as Chairperson earlier in 2023.

 

• NGT's principal bench is located in New Delhi with regional benches in Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NGT has the power to hear all civil cases involving substantial environmental questions relating to the implementation of various environmental Acts.

 

NOTE

 

• Lokeshwar Singh Panta (Option 1): An earlier NGT Chairperson (around 2011-12), but not the incumbent as of March 2024.

 

• Ajay Narayan Jha (Option 3): Not associated with the NGT Chairperson position.

 

• Swatanter Kumar (Option 4): A former Chairperson of NGT (2012-2017), not the incumbent as of March 2024.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, most people had out-migrated from _____ to other states in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011 migration data, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar recorded the highest net out-migration to other states in India. (सर्वाधिक प्रवासन — उत्तर प्रदेश और बिहार)

 

• Migrants from these states predominantly moved to states like Maharashtra, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab in search of employment and better economic opportunities.

 

• Economic Survey data has also corroborated UP and Bihar as the largest source states for inter-state labour migration in India.

 

• Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat, conversely, have historically been the largest recipient (in-migration) states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census defines a migrant as a person enumerated at a place other than their place of birth/last residence.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan and Gujarat (Option 2): Gujarat is more a destination state; not the top out-migration pair.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): While UP is correct, Madhya Pradesh is not the paired top out-migration state — Bihar is.

 

• Maharashtra and Gujarat (Option 4): Both are major destination (in-migration) states, not out-migration states.

question: National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS) is located at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS) is located at Dirang, in the West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh. (निमास — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It was established under the Ministry of Defence to promote mountaineering, adventure sports and related training in the northeastern region.

 

• NIMAS conducts basic and advanced mountaineering courses, along with courses in skiing, water sports, para-sports and other adventure disciplines.

 

• It plays a key role in encouraging youth from the Northeast towards adventure sports and defence-related careers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent mountaineering institutes in India include the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering (Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand) and the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute (Darjeeling, West Bengal).

 

NOTE

 

• Mizoram (Option 1), Nagaland (Option 2), Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): While these states have their own adventure/sports institutions, NIMAS is specifically located in Arunachal Pradesh.

question: How many squares are there on a chessboard?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 64.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A standard chessboard has 8 rows and 8 columns, giving 8 × 8 = 64 individual unit squares. (शतरंज बोर्ड के वर्ग — 64)

 

• These 64 squares alternate between light and dark colours in a checkered pattern.

 

• Each of the two players starts with 16 pieces placed on these squares, occupying the first two rows on their respective sides.

 

• (Note: if squares of every possible size, from 1×1 up to the full 8×8 board, are counted together, the total comes to 204 — but the standard understanding of "squares on a chessboard" refers to the 64 individual playing squares, as reflected by the given options.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chess is played on this 64-square board, with columns called "files" (a-h) and rows called "ranks" (1-8).

 

NOTE

 

• 69 (Option 1), 67 (Option 2), 68 (Option 3): These are incorrect counts; none corresponds to the actual number of unit squares (64) on a standard chessboard.

question: In which part of the Constitution will you find the six broad categories of Fundamental Rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35). (मौलिक अधिकार — भाग III)

 

• They are classified into six broad categories: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• Originally there were seven categories; the Right to Property was removed from Part III by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300-A instead.

 

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning citizens can approach the courts (Article 32/226) directly for their enforcement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part IV of the Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable.

 

NOTE

 

• Part II (Option 1): Deals with Citizenship (Articles 5-11).

 

• Part IV (Option 3): Deals with Directive Principles of State Policy, not Fundamental Rights.

 

• Part I (Option 4): Deals with the Union and its territory (Articles 1-4).

question: The financial year in India starts from 1st April and ends on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31st March.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian financial year (fiscal year) runs from 1st April to 31st March of the following calendar year. (वित्तीय वर्ष — 31 मार्च)

 

• The Union Budget is presented for this financial year cycle, typically on 1 February each year.

 

• This April-March cycle was inherited from British-era administrative practice and continues to be followed for government accounts, taxation and most corporate accounting in India.

 

• A committee (the Justice Shah Committee) had earlier examined the option of shifting to a January-December fiscal year, but the April-March cycle continues.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Many other countries, such as the USA, follow a different fiscal year (e.g., October to September for the US federal government).

 

NOTE

 

• 30th June (Option 1), 31st July (Option 3), 31st May (Option 4): None of these mark the end of India's financial year; it consistently ends on 31st March.

question: What is the balance of trade of a country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Difference between imports and exports.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The balance of trade (BOT), also called the trade balance, is defined as the difference between the monetary value of a country's exports and imports over a given period. (व्यापार संतुलन — आयात-निर्यात का अंतर)

 

• A positive balance of trade (trade surplus) occurs when exports exceed imports; a negative balance (trade deficit) occurs when imports exceed exports.

 

• Balance of trade is a key component of a country's Balance of Payments (BOP), specifically forming part of the current account.

 

• India has generally run a trade deficit in recent years, importing more (especially crude oil and gold) than it exports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balance of Payments (BOP) is a broader concept than balance of trade, covering all economic transactions (goods, services, capital transfers) between a country and the rest of the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Ratio of international trade (Option 1): Not the definition of balance of trade; trade balance is a difference, not a ratio.

 

• Number of exports (Option 2): Considers only exports in isolation, ignoring imports.

 

• Number of imports (Option 4): Considers only imports in isolation, ignoring exports.

question: The peninsular plateau of India was a part of which continent earlier?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Peninsular Plateau of India is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth, originally part of the ancient supercontinent Gondwanaland, and was earlier attached to the African continent before continental drift. (प्रायद्वीपीय पठार — अफ्रीका महाद्वीप)

 

• It is composed mainly of ancient igneous and metamorphic rocks (gneisses and granites), characteristic of very old, stable landmasses.

 

• The plateau broke away from Gondwanaland along with other landmasses (Africa, South America, Australia and Antarctica) due to continental drift, eventually drifting to its present position and colliding with the Eurasian plate to help form the Himalayas.

 

• The plateau is triangular in shape, bounded by the Aravalli Range in the northwest, Rajmahal Hills in the northeast, and the Mahadev, Kaimur and Maikal ranges in the north, merging with the Deccan Plateau in the south.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Peninsular Plateau consists of two broad divisions: the Central Highlands (north of the Narmada) and the Deccan Plateau (south of the Narmada).

 

NOTE

 

• South America (Option 1), North America (Option 4): These landmasses were part of Gondwanaland (or, for North America, of the separate Laurasia supercontinent), but the Indian Peninsular Plateau's closest ancient association among the given options is with Africa.

 

• Europe (Option 2): Europe was part of Laurasia, a separate supercontinent from Gondwanaland, and is not associated with the Peninsular Plateau's origin.

question: In which year did Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted and Thomas Martin Lowry propose the fundamental concept of acids and bases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1923.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brønsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases was independently proposed in 1923 by the Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted and the English chemist Thomas Martin Lowry. (अम्ल-क्षार सिद्धांत — 1923)

 

• According to this theory, an acid is defined as a proton (H⁺) donor, and a base is defined as a proton acceptor.

 

• This theory expanded on the earlier Arrhenius concept of acids and bases (which was limited to aqueous solutions) by allowing acid-base behaviour to be described even in non-aqueous solvents.

 

• It introduced the concept of conjugate acid-base pairs, where a base gains a proton to form its conjugate acid, and an acid loses a proton to form its conjugate base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A further, more general theory of acids and bases — the Lewis theory (electron pair donor/acceptor) — was proposed by Gilbert N. Lewis, also around the same period (1923).

 

NOTE

 

• 1928 (Option 1), 1921 (Option 2), 1925 (Option 3): These years do not correspond to the actual proposal of the Brønsted-Lowry theory, which was published in 1923.
